messages:
Maria G.: noticed p95/token-gen latency spike in private-us-west around 08:10 UTC, affects Dedicated->Private routing. p50 went 30ms -> 200ms, p95 400ms -> 1.2s. Root cause unclear yet.
Raj P.: on it. any signs of kernel-selector churn or batching changes around that time?
Maria G.: yes we have a few canaries from a kernel-selector rollout at 07:58 but looked small. also some NAT alerts from infra.
Alex T.: I pulled a quick perf snapshot from one of the slow nodes. sys time jumped; ksoftirq and kworker increase. conntrack count looks high. snippet:
```
# perf top (sample)
  35.2%  __ip_local_out
  18.1%  nf_conntrack_in
  12.4%  kv_cache_lookup
  7.9%   schedule
```
Caveat: sampling interval short but consistent across hosts.
Carmen L.: KV cache metrics show miss rate spiked 8% -> 62% at same time. heatmap shows a wide tail of prefix variations. kernel-selector may have caused model variant churn -> kvcache cold starts.
infra-oncall: nat-1 saturated ephemeral ports 10:05-10:18 UTC (conntrack ~680k on the node). We had some transient SNAT rejections logged (port allocation failures).
Raj P.: that could explain increased retries and TCP connection churn hitting kernel paths (nf_conntrack, ip_local_out). if connections drop we get more reconnects and more unique prefixes -> kv churn.
Maria G.: can we validate whether kernel-selector flip correlated with traffic shifting between kernels (and consequently different model shard ids)?
Alex T.: yes, checking selector logs now. Found rotation events 07:59 and 08:03 where ~12% of requests were re-routed to the fallback q4/q8 path due to an autoswitch heuristic when queue depth exceeded threshold. That caused a bimodal distribution of request shapes.
Carmen L.: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) pin kernel-selector to the stable q8 for private deployment (prevent oscillation), 2) increase KV cache size + warm keys for hot prefixes, 3) throttle kernel switch rate (cooldown).
infra-oncall: temporary infra mitigation applied: expanded NAT ephemeral port range + bumped conntrack max to 1.2M on affected nodes, added a targeted SNAT pool for private clusters. Also added a short conntrack timeout reduction for idle UDP (where safe).
Maria G.: thanks. can someone push a quick patch to runtime config to disable selector autoswitch for private clusters while we investigate?
Raj P.: I pushed a rollback of autoswitch flag to stable for private/us-west at 08:25 UTC: config: 
```json
{"kernel_selector": {"autoswitch": false, "pinned_kernel": "q8-avx2"}}
```
Rollout confirmed across the fleet within ~90s.
perf-bot: Alert resolved: latency curve returned to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback. p95 back to ~420ms. Notifying SLO channel.
Alex T.: follow-up profiling shows sys hotspots reduced, kv miss rate trending down. conntrack count decreased after NAT pool expansion.
Carmen L.: next action items:
- add telemetry for kernelSelector decisions to Console (per-request label)
- add KV warmup for small-hot prefixes on kernel switches
- tighten batching heuristic to avoid aggressive autoscaling of batch sizes during oscillation (prefer stable batch sizes when kernel switch rate > X/min)
- add e2e test for egress port saturation impact on request patterns
Maria G.: will owner the incident postmortem. Ill open PRs for kernel pin + batching change and a runbook item for NAT pool scaling. tagging @infra-oncall for follow-up on permanent SNAT capacity.
infra-oncall: acknowledged. we will schedule a capacity bump and review firewall NAT masquerade rules; also audit any MSS/MTU weirdness on the path (no evidence yet, but will check).
Maria G.: great. thanks all :thumbsup:
